\section[la solidaridad]{la solidaridad — the solidarity}

\label{lesson:ES-C606-solidaridad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the racism, then the Spanish for the corruption.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la solidaridad}
\textbf{la solidaridad} — \textquotedblleft{}the solidarity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Necesitamos más solidaridad.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We need more solidarity.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Solidario} — caring, ready to help.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{solidaridad} is built on \emph{solidario} with \emph{-idad} (EtymDB); \emph{solidario} was borrowed from French \emph{solidaire}, from Latin \emph{solidus} 'whole, firm'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la solidaridad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la solidaridad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la solidaridad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the racism, then the Spanish for the corruption, then say \emph{la solidaridad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la solidaridad mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The solidarity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el voluntariado]{el voluntariado — the volunteering; the volunteers}

\label{lesson:ES-C606-voluntariado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the corruption, then the Spanish for the solidarity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el voluntariado}
\textbf{el voluntariado} — \textquotedblleft{}the volunteering; the volunteers\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hago voluntariado los fines de semana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do volunteering at weekends.}
\end{quote}

It also means all the volunteers together.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{voluntariado} is built on \emph{voluntario}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{voluntarius} 'willing', from \emph{voluntas} and \emph{velle} 'to want' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el voluntariado}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el voluntariado}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el voluntariado}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the corruption, then the Spanish for the solidarity, then say \emph{el voluntariado} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la asociación]{la asociación — the association, the society}

\label{lesson:ES-C606-asociacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the solidarity, then the Spanish for the volunteering.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la asociación}
\textbf{la asociación} — \textquotedblleft{}the association, the society\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es miembro de una asociación de vecinos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She is a member of a residents' association.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Asociarse} — to join together.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asociación} is built on \emph{asociar}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{associare} 'to join to', built on \emph{socius} 'companion' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la caridad]{la caridad — the charity}

\label{lesson:ES-C606-caridad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the volunteering, then the Spanish for the association.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la caridad}
\textbf{la caridad} — \textquotedblleft{}the charity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dan dinero a obras de caridad.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They give money to charity.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Pedir caridad} — to beg.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{caridad} comes from Latin \emph{cāritās}, \emph{cāritātem} 'dearness, love', built on \emph{cārus} 'dear' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[participar]{participar — to take part, to participate}

\label{lesson:ES-C606-participar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the association, then the Spanish for the charity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: participar}
\textbf{participar} — \textquotedblleft{}to take part, to participate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Quiero participar en el proyecto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I want to take part in the project.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Participar en} something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{participar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{participare} 'to share in', built on \emph{particeps}, from \emph{pars} 'part' and \emph{capere} 'to take' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{participar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the association, then the Spanish for the charity, then say \emph{participar} again
\end{itemize}
